facts.raw_span: a two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension
denied pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms
no personal or family history of cancer
BMI was 20.5 kg/m2
blood pressure 125/85 mmHg
pulse 89/min
SpO2 95% on room air
abdomen was markedly distended with a palpable mass rising approximately 3 cm above the umbilicus
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile (MCV 73.2 fL)

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava
